title: Patchwork garter squares throw
subtitle: A 100 by 120 cm lap throw from 48 small garter squares in assorted DK colours.
excerpt: A 100 by 120 cm lap throw assembled from 48 small 12 cm garter squares in assorted DK colours, arranged in an eight-by-six grid and joined by mattress stitch. Each square uses about 20 g and is worked independently. A practical stash-busting project.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Knitter, 4th series (1888), §Patchwork Knitting, documents small garter squares joined by over-casting as a standard Victorian needlework project for using remnants. The mattress-stitch join is described in later editions.

knitting.gaugeText: 22 sts × 44 rows = 10 × 10 cm in garter stitch on 4 mm needles. Each square: 26 sts × 52 rows = 12 cm × 12 cm.
knitting.finishedSizeText: 100 cm wide × 120 cm long (8 squares wide × 6 squares tall, each 12 cm sq plus seam allowance).

stitchCountCheckpoints.label: Square midpoint — 26 sts at row 26 (about 6 cm)

glossaryTerms.definition: The simplest knitted square: cast on a number of stitches, knit every row until the length equals the width (a garter swatch is exactly square when the stitch count equals the row count divided by 2, because garter rows are taller than they are wide), then cast off. No pattern memory is required; every row is plain knit.

content.text: worked flat on 4 mm needles in assorted DK colours and joined by mattress stitch into an eight-square by six-square 100 by 120 cm lap throw.

A portable project: each square takes about 20 minutes and uses about 20 g of DK. The throw is ideal for using leftover DK yarn; no two squares need to match. Budget about 960 g total (20 g per square × 48 squares), though the exact weight per square depends on the colour and yarn brand. Work squares in any order; plan the colour arrangement before joining. Each square in isolation is a beginner project; the intermediate element is the mattress-stitch joining of 48 pieces.

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: About 20 g per square × 48 squares = 960 g total in DK weight. Any mix of colours; leftovers and stash yarn are ideal.

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 4 mm (UK 8 / US 6) straight needles (or short circular, 40 cm or longer)

content.text: 22 stitches and 44 rows to 10 cm in garter stitch on 4 mm needles. Each 12 cm square uses 26 stitches and 52 rows. Garter rows are taller than they are wide: 44 rows per 10 cm vs 22 stitches per 10 cm, the square will be exact when the number of rows is exactly double the number of stitches (26 × 2 = 52 rows).
If your garter gauge is 20 per 10 cm, cast on 24 stitches and work 48 rows for the same 12 cm square.

Using any colour and the long-tail cast-on, cast on 26 stitches. Long-tail tail: (4 × 26) / 10 + 15 = 10.4 + 15 = 25.4 cm. Measure 30 cm. Knit every row for 52 rows, then cast off knitwise with a relaxed tension. Each square should measure 12 cm × 12 cm.
At row 26 (about 6 cm): count across. You should have 26 stitches. At row 52 (12 cm): count again before casting off. Garter squares never gain or lose stitches.

Squares measuring 12 cm × 13 cm or 11 cm × 12 cm: the row gauge differs from the stitch gauge, the square is a rectangle. Either adjust needle size, or work to a measured 12 cm in each direction rather than to row count.
Joined squares puckering at the seams: too many or too few row bars were caught in the mattress stitch. Pick up one garter ridge (one loop) per seam stitch and work at a relaxed tension.

Lay out 48 squares in an 8-by-6 grid on a flat surface and plan the colour arrangement. Join squares into rows of 8 using mattress stitch on the long side edges, then join the 6 rows together along the short edges.
Weave in all ends from each square. Lay flat, smooth to shape, and leave to settle.
Machine wash on a gentle 30-degree cycle for superwash DK. If using non-superwash yarn, hand wash and lay flat to dry. The garter structure is stable and will not distort with washing.

From plain garter squares, try mitered squares next. Use the same size, weight, and needles. Work each square from the outside corner inward with a centre decrease. This adds a diagonal visual element with no new yarn or tools.
